review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new definition is `localL2Energy s u := ∫ x in s, ‖u x‖ ^ 2`. It equals `lpNorm u 2 (volume.restrict s) ^ 2`, where Mathlib's `lpNorm` is `(eLpNorm f p μ).toReal`. That makes it a specialisation of an existing norm, not a separate concept. It is a squared set-integral energy on `L2`, and its integral form is what the proofs use directly: `integral_mono_ae`, `setIntegral_const`, `setIntegral_le_integral`. Replacing it with `lpNorm` on the restricted measure would not clearly help any use. I did not search Mathlib for an existing "local energy" notion beyond `lpNorm`/`eLpNorm`. The other declarations are theorems, and the rubric excludes duplicate theorem statements. I did not check whether `norm_add_sq_le_twice` repeats a Mathlib lemma, because that would be a theorem duplicate. I did not check how other files use `localL2Energy`, so I can't rule out a benefit from migrating those callers.
